full_judgment:
Abu Bakar Siddiquee J: This Criminal appeal under section 10 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 is directed against the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 02-7-1992 passed by the learned Judge of the Special Tribunal No. 4, Dhaka in Special Case No. 17 of 1991 arising out of Motijheel PS Case No. 65(1)91 corresponding to DAB GR No. 12 of 1991, convicting the appellant under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and sentencing him to suffer simple imprisonment for 3(three) years and also to pay a fine of Taka 6,00,000, in default to suffer SI for 6(six) months more. 

 3. One MA Mannan an Officer of Anti-Corruption on 29-1-1991 as informant lodged the FIR with the Motijheel Police Station against the convict-appellant alleging inter-alia that in course of rendering service as Chairman of Bangladesh Chemical Industries Corporation hereinafter called BCIC, the convict-appellant on the basis of a contract dated 12-4-1988 appointed as Secretary, Ministry of Industry and joined his new post on 13-4-1988. It has been further alleged that the convict-appellant requested the Chairman, BCIC to provide him with pay and allowance at the rate, he used to draw as Chairman of the same subject to adjustment till execution of his contract with the Government. It has been also alleged that the convict-appellant received Taka 2,89,130.61 towards pay and allowances, Taka 2,75,319 towards Foreign Tours and the sum total of which is amounting to Taka 5,64,449.61. It has been further alleged that the convict-appellant subsequently received Taka 3,11,932.65 as pay and allowance and Taka 2,20,217.91 as Foreign Tours allowances and total of which is Taka 5,32,149.56 for the contracted same period as Secretary with-out adjusting the previous received money. It has been further alleged that the convict-appellant within his knowledge received money from two places illegally and misappropriated the amount of BCIC and thereby abused his power and illegally obtained pecuniary advantage. Hence, the case. 

 13. PW 1, Md. Abdul Mannan is the informant as well as investigating officer of this case. He deposed that on the basis of a secret information in the year 1990, he lodged the FIR alleging that during the service of the convict-appellant as Chairman, BCIC, he obtained a contract service as Secretary. He also deposed that after his joining in the new post, he asked his Personal Secretary to write a letter to the Chairman, BCIC for affording his salary and other allowances from the fund of BCIC subject to adjustment till execution of contract with the Government but he had no authority to ask BCIC for allowing him any sorts of benefit. Thereafter, he deposed that the convict-appellant withdrew the entire salary and benefit from the fund of his ministry, he quit his service but he has not adjust the aforesaid money and thereby committed the offence of misappropriation. Thereafter, he deposed that he went to the relevant office and made a search and also seized some documents from the BCIC office and prepared a seizure I is of the same. Thereafter, he deposed that after enquiry, it has came to his notice that the convict-appellant under the order of the then President, People's Republic of Bangladesh was appointed as Secretary, Ministry of Industries for a period of three years and accordingly he joined there on 13-4-1988. He also deposed that he 'the convict-appellant obtained Taka 2,89,130.61 as his salary and also took Taka 2,75,319 as tour advance and total amount of which is Taka 5,64,449.61 from the BCIC He further depose that he withdrew Taka 3,11,432.62 as salary and Taka 2,20,212 and total Taka 5,31,650.56 from the Ministry of Industries as his salary and other benefits. Thereafter, he deposed that the convict-appellant rendered his service from 13-8-1988 to 28-2-1990 as Secretary, Ministry of Industries and abuse his power on withdrawal of his salary from two separate authority and thereby misappropriated Taka 5,64,449.61. Finally he deposed that he lodged the FIR against the convict-appellant for committing the offence punishable under section 409 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. 

 16. PW 2, Md Abdul Latif Miah is an accountant attached to Accounts Office of the BCIC. He deposed that he has been rendering his service in BCIC since 19-7-1973. He also deposed that the convict-appellant serve as Chairman, BCIC till 1980 and thereafter he joined his contract service on 13-4-1988 as Secretary, Ministry of Industries. Thereafter, he deposed that the investigating officer rushed to his office on 09-1-1991 and made a search and seized some documents and he put his signature on the seizure list. He also stated that he kept those documents in his custody on executing a Zimmanama. Thereafter, he deposed that on 5-5-1988, he received a letter from the PS of the convict-appellant addressing the Chairman, BCIC contending that the BCIC is to pay the salary and other benefits to him till execution of contract in between him and the Government. Thereafter, he deposed the BCIC is a corporation under the active management of the Ministry of Industries. He further deposed that the convict-appellant was allowed to pay his salaries, TA and DA etc from their fund. Thereafter, he deposed that on 02-1-1990 the memo of contract was signed in between the convict-appellant and Government and the convict-appellant rendered his service as Secretary, Ministry of Industries till 28-2-1990. He further deposed till that period he was allowed to withdraw a sum of Taka 1,36,920 as salary and dearness allowance amounting to Taka 13,972, entertainment allowance 5,650, Bonus 19,255, Medical Allowance 958 total amount of which was 2,11,226.83. He proved the seizure list before the Court which has been marked as Exhibit-1 series. 

 17. In Course of cross-examination, he deposed that Chairman is the highest post in BCIC and there are two separate departments in it namely Accounts and Finance. He further deposed that the deed of those two departments are be controlled by the Chairman. Thereafter, lie deposed that he opened BCIC account in Arab Bangladesh Bank where from the officer of the BCIC are being obtained their salaries. Thereafter, it is admitted by him that the salaries and allowances which was allowed to the convict-appellant during the period under report was duly approved by the Chairman as an advance. It is also admitted by him that the fund of Ministry of Industries and BCIC are the separate and there is no scope to adjust the amount obtained by the convict-appellant from BCIC from the fund of Government. It is also admitted by him that there are Board of Directors who served under the Chairman of BCIC. It is also admitted by him that the pay and condition of repayment of the salary to the convict-appellant was not ascertained at the time of such payment. He further deposed that after cancellation of his contract service, the convict-appellant again joined in BCIC as Chairman. He denied the suggestion put to him during the course of cross-examination. 

 23. In his course of his cross-examination, he deposed that he himself and one Moniruzzaman kept those seized document in their custody on executing a Zimmanama. He also deposed that after joining in the contracted service, they managed to take the telephone of the convict under supervision of the Government telephone and, as such, he has no limit in using such facilities. He denied the suggestion put to him during the course of cross-examination. 

 24. PW 6, Md Moniruzzaman Miah is a Section Assistant, attached to Ministry of Industry. He deposed that on 13-4-1988, the convict-appellant joined as Secretary in their Ministry on contract basis and he served there till December, 1990. He also deposed that contract in between him and government was signed on 02-9- 90 and he withdrew his salary and other benefits from 13.040.88 to 28-2-90 at a time from the fund of ministry of Industry. He further deposed that after signing of construct, he withdrew Taka 3,65,409.06 as TA. Thereafter, he deposed that he withdrew Taka 84,716 on 08-3-89, Taka 2,06,897 on 29-8-89 and Taka 37,931 on 04-10-89 as TA advance from the fund of BCIC. He further depose that he cannot say as to whether the convict-appellant at all refunded the BCIC money which was taken by him as an advance. He also deposed that after expiry of contracted period, he again joined in BCIC as Chairman. 

 32. In his cross-examination, he deposed that auditor Babor Ali was entrusted with the task of preparing the pay bill matter of the convict-appellant. He also deposed that there is no way to adjust in between the Government and the corporation but there is a provision to adjust the public fund in case of excess withdrawal. He also deposed that the investigating officer recorded his 161 statement. 

 43. PW-16, Md Rabiul Haq was being served as Private Secretary to the convict-appellant at the relevant time. He deposed that the convict-appellant served under their Ministry as Secretary on contract basis from 13-4-1988 to 9-12-1990. He further deposed that after his joining as Secretary, he instructed him to write a letter to the Chairman, BCIC to allow his salary from their fund since no contract has signed in between him and the Government specifying the term and condition of his contract service and accordingly he wrote it. He further deposed that accordingly the BCIC allowed him to withdraw his salary and, other benefits from their fund and thereafter convict-appellant has withdraw his salary and other benefits from the fund of Ministry of Industry. He further deposed that he prepared a note sheet for collecting TA from BCIC for the purpose of a tour towards Hongkong. He also deposed that he collected Taka 31,287 from BCIC for the purpose of tour to Tokyo. He identified 22 pay bills and 4 festival allowance bill through which the convict- appellant was paid his bill which has been marked as material Exhibit 11 series by the trial court. 

 64. It was the duty of the convict-appellant to write both the organizations to make adjustment after signing contract with the Government for the purpose of his contract service since he has already withdraw his salary and other benefits from his parent department but instead of doing so, the convict-appellant withdraw the entire benefit of his contract service and kept in his custody which can be termed as abuse of his position as public servant. 

 The period of one year is available in section 234 of the Code of Criminal Procedure but it is absent in section 6(1 B) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act and thereby in view of the provision laid down in section 6(1) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 section 6(1 B) excludes the application of section 234 which relates to the period of the commission of the alleged offence." 

 72. The learned Advocate Mr Khan on behalf of the ACC argued that the trial court has dismissed their claim so far as it relates to misappropriation and they have not filed any cross appeal against such order of dismissal and, as such, they have no claim about misappropriation of Government fund. But he strenuously argued that the convict-appellant conclusively abused his official power as secretary on asking his PS to write out such letter Exhibit Kha(1) and withdraw the money from BCIC as his salary and other benefits. He adds that there was no earthly reason to withdraw the salary and other benefit as has been allowed to him for the purpose of contract service since he has already withdraw the same from his parent organization and this sorts of withdrawal amounts to abuse his official position as public servant and also an indication of dishonest intention in the same manner which he uttered in course of his examination under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to the effect that দুই জায়গা বেতন নেয়া বেআইনী হয় নাই”
